source_name: YouControl Market — catalogue of Ukrainian companies (Каталог компаній України)
why_relevant: Open-facing catalogue layer over YouControl covering ~7m entities; usable to enumerate banks, payment institutions, financial companies and their branches by activity code and region without a full YouControl licence.

source_name: Opendatabot — company monitoring and public-register service (Опендатабот)
why_relevant: Normalises and republishes financial statements (revenue, net profit, assets, liabilities) for ~430k Ukrainian companies plus USREOU registration data, changes history since 2016, court and tax registers. Company cards exist for payment-sector entities (e.g. ТОВ «Українська платіжна система»), making it both an archive of filings and an enumerator of payment/banking legal entities.

source_name: Opendatabot API documentation (docs.opendatabot.com)
why_relevant: Technical entry point describing which public registers are machine-readable through Opendatabot (USREOU/ЄДР, tax, court, sanctions), needed to design a repeatable collection pipeline for bank and payment-institution filings.

source_name: Clarity Project — analytical platform for counterparty checks (аналітична платформа Clarity Project)
why_relevant: Combines 140+ registers, courts, Prozorro procurement and financial analytics into per-EDRPOU company pages; has live pages for major Ukrainian banks (PrivatBank 14360570, Credit Agricole 14361575, Bank of Investments and Savings 33695095). Uniquely strong on procurement links, which reveal bank/PSP contracts with the state — an indirect market-share signal.

source_name: Vkursi.pro — open-data and counterparty-check platform (VKURSI.PRO)
source_subtype: big-data company intelligence platform with API
why_relevant: Explicitly positioned toward banks, insurers and primary financial-monitoring entities; publishes company financial statements and offers segmentation of companies by KVED, region, revenue, profit/loss and assets — directly usable to size the Ukrainian banking/payments company population and rank players.

source_name: USR / ЄДР free search — Ministry of Justice electronic services portal
why_relevant: The authoritative primary register of Ukrainian legal entities. Free, no-registration lookup by name or identification code gives the legally definitive registration record (status, legal form, address, management, activities) for every bank and payment institution — the ground truth against which aggregator data should be reconciled.

source_name: ЄДР open dataset on data.gov.ua (Unified State Register bulk open data)
why_relevant: Bulk, free, machine-readable dump of the USREOU covering all legal entities, FOPs and branches of foreign-law entities. Reported restored in January 2026 after the wartime 2022 restriction, with weekly updates — this is the single most efficient way to enumerate every registered bank and payment company and track ownership changes over time.

source_name: SE NAIS (ДП «НАІС») — state register operator publishing ЄДР open data
why_relevant: NAIS is the technical administrator of the USREOU; its site is the alternative publication point for the ЄДР open-data files referenced in the Ministry of Justice announcements, and the authority on formats, cut-off dates and withheld categories.

source_name: GLEIF LEI Search — Global LEI Index
why_relevant: Free, registration-free lookup of the full LEI data pool. Filtering by country UA yields the authoritative cross-border identity record for Ukrainian banks and financial entities (legal name, legal form, registered address, registration authority — often the NBU, entity status, LEI renewal status). Provides the key that links Ukrainian EDRPOU codes to international financial datasets.

source_name: GLEIF Golden Copy and Delta Files (bulk LEI Level 1 + Level 2 data)
why_relevant: Bulk downloadable LEI-CDF (Level 1, 'who is who') and RR-CDF (Level 2, 'who owns whom') files plus a download API. Enables systematic extraction of all UA-jurisdiction financial entities and their direct/ultimate accounting-consolidating parents — the cleanest machine-readable ownership backbone for Ukrainian bank groups and foreign-owned PSPs.

source_name: GLEIF LEI Issuers (LOU) directory for Ukraine
why_relevant: Identifies which Local Operating Units / registration agents actually issue LEIs to Ukrainian entities — useful for understanding coverage bias in the UA LEI population and for locating secondary LEI lookup services that mirror the data.

source_name: Bloomberg LEI lookup — mirror of LEI records (example: АТ «ОТП БАНК»)
why_relevant: Third-party LOU-operated LEI viewer that mirrors GLEIF records for Ukrainian banks (e.g. OTP Bank, LEI 5299003XXPWL6O33R633, registration authority National Bank of Ukraine). Useful as a fallback view when GLEIF endpoints are rate-limited, and confirms NBU as the registration authority used in LEI records for UA banks.

source_name: SMIDA — NSSMC securities market information database (Загальнодоступна інформаційна база даних НКЦПФР)
why_relevant: The statutory filing archive for issuers, holding regular and irregular disclosure from ~20,000 issuers since 2003. Ukrainian banks are joint-stock companies and therefore file annual issuer reports here (deadline 30 April), including bank-specific report forms — this preserves annual reports and financial statements independently of a bank's own website.

source_name: stockmarket.gov.ua — NSSMC general public information database
why_relevant: Parallel/companion public database to SMIDA carrying the NSSMC disclosure feed, ESKRIN system, register of securities issues and holders of significant (10%+) stakes — the latter is a direct source on bank shareholder structures.

source_name: edrpou.ubki.ua — UBCI (Українське бюро кредитних історій) company register and business-reputation service
why_relevant: Credit-bureau-operated register front-end with per-EDRPOU pages for Ukrainian banks (e.g. Ukrgasbank 23697280, Oschadbank 00032129). Distinctive because it layers credit-bureau signals (credit status, history of interaction with banks) on top of registry data — an indirect indicator channel not available from pure open-data aggregators.

source_name: Diia.Business news channel on register/open-data policy changes
why_relevant: Government business portal that announces changes to register accessibility (e.g. the restoration of ЄДР open data and which categories remain closed). Essential meta-source for knowing when a collection pipeline's upstream availability changes.

source_name: YouControl newsroom / analytics on financial-statement disclosure
why_relevant: YouControl and open-data advocates publicly campaign on the availability of company financial statements; their newsroom documents when statement disclosure is opened or restricted, which directly governs whether bank/PSP financials are collectible in a given period.

source_name: Opendatabot analytics — open financial statements rankings
why_relevant: Opendatabot publishes derived analytics naming the largest Ukrainian businesses by disclosed financial statements. Useful as a fast cross-check on which financial-sector entities are in the top revenue/asset cohorts and whether their statements are actually present in the open dataset.

source_name: Ukrstat EDRPOU administrative-services pages (Держстат, регіональні управління)
why_relevant: The State Statistics Service maintains the EDRPOU statistical register layer (activity codes, organisational-legal form, territorial classification) and provides administrative services around EDRPOU extracts — relevant for reconciling KVED classification of banks and payment companies and for the statistical universe of financial-sector entities.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — CDX Server API (domain-level capture index)
why_relevant: The single highest-leverage entry point for this cell: lets you enumerate every archived URL under a Ukrainian bank/PSP domain (url=privatbank.ua/*), filter mimetype=application/pdf and statuscode=200, and recover pre-2022 annual reports and IR pages whose live URLs are now 404 or whose sites were taken down/relocated. Supports date ranges so you can pin a pre-invasion baseline (e.g. to=20220223).

source_name: Wayback Machine Availability API (nearest-capture lookup)
why_relevant: Cheap liveness/continuity check: for any Ukrainian bank or PSP IR URL that no longer resolves, returns the nearest archived snapshot and its timestamp. Ideal for triaging a list of disclosure URLs into 'live', 'dead-but-archived', 'never captured'.

source_name: SUCHO — Saving Ukrainian Cultural Heritage Online (5,400+ archived Ukrainian sites, ~50TB)
why_relevant: Largest wartime crawl of the .ua web outside the Internet Archive, built with Browsertrix/ArchiveWeb.page from March 2022 and mirrored outside Ukraine. Primarily cultural institutions, so bank IR coverage is likely incidental rather than systematic — but it is the main non-IA repository of Ukrainian WARCs, and its crawl seed lists and methodology are a template for a banking-sector crawl.

source_name: Archive-It (Internet Archive) — curated Ukraine/Russo-Ukrainian war collections
why_relevant: Institutional partners (universities, IIPC Content Development Group) ran themed Ukraine crawls from 2014 and 2022; Archive-It exposes its own CDX/C API for per-collection index queries. Potential route to captures the public Wayback front-end does not surface conveniently, including 2014 Crimea/Donbas-era .ua sites.

source_name: archive.today / archive.ph — on-demand snapshots
why_relevant: Second-opinion archive with a different capture model (rendered snapshot + screenshot) and different robots policy from IA. Reported as the most-used open archiving service among fact-checkers covering the Russo-Ukrainian war, so it holds ad-hoc captures of Ukrainian bank/PSP press releases that IA may have missed, and it is the fallback for pages IA excludes.

source_name: NBU — Information on banks since 2014 (reorganisation/liquidation history)
why_relevant: The authoritative continuity register: dates of NBU insolvency decisions and DGF temporary administration/liquidation from 2014 onward. This is the actor list for the whole cell — it names the banks whose disclosure channels have died (2014 Crimea/Donbas wave and the post-2022 wave) and therefore which domains must be recovered from archives.

source_name: Deposit Guarantee Fund (ФГВФО) — Banks under liquidation
why_relevant: For a failed Ukrainian bank the DGF becomes the de facto custodian of its disclosure: liquidation-stage reporting, asset inventories, valuation results and liquidation-mass data survive here after the bank's own site disappears. This is the offline-mirror analogue for dead institutions.

source_name: ФГВФО — Archive of the list of member banks (Архів переліку банків-учасників)
why_relevant: An explicit, dated ARCHIVE section: point-in-time membership snapshots of the banking population. Diffing consecutive snapshots gives an exact timeline of which banks vanished and when — the backbone series for continuity tracking, and a dated actor map for pre-2022 baselines.
